7. What happen to the reactivity of non-metal when its size increases? Why?
Ans:- When the size of a non-metal increases, its reactivity decreases, because the attraction between the nucleus and the
outermost electrons becomes weaker, so the tendency to gain electrons decreases.
8. Potassium is more reactive than sodium althrough they both belong to the same group. Why?
Ans:- Potassium is more reactive than sodium although both belong to the same group because potassium has a larger atomic
size and greater shielding effect, so its valence electron is lost more easily, making potassium more reactive than sodium.

10. Write two characteristics of s-block elements.
Ans:- Two characteristics of s-block elements are,
1. They have one or two electrons in their outermost shell (valence electrons in the s-orbital).
2. They are highly electropositive metals and easily lose electrons to form positive ions.
11. Atomic size of inert gases do not affect inertness, why?
Ans:- The atomic size of inert gases does not affect their inertness because they have a completely filled valence shell (stable
electronic configuration), so they have no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons, regardless of their atomic size.
12. Write any two features of Mendeleev’s periodic table.
Ans:- Two features of Mendeleev’s periodic table are.
1. Elements were arranged in the increasing order of their atomic masses.
2. Elements with similar chemical properties were placed in the same group, showing periodic repetition of properties.
13. Among magnesium and calcium, which elements is more reactive? Give reason.
Ans:- Calcium is more reactive than magnesium because calcium has a larger atomic size and its valence electrons are farther
from the nucleus, so they are lost more easily, increasing its reactivity compared to magnesium.
14. Alkali metals are more reactive, why?
Ans:- Alkali metals are more reactive because they have only one electron in their outermost shell, which is loosely held and
can be easily lost to form a stable ion, making them highly reactive.
15. Write any two reasons that hydrogen is kept in group IA in periodic table.
Ans:- Two reasons why hydrogen is kept in Group IA of the periodic table are,
1. Hydrogen has one electron in its outermost shell, similar to alkali metals.
2. Like alkali metals, hydrogen can lose one electron to form a positive ion (H⁺).
16. Which one is more reactive between fluorine and chlorine? Why?
Ans:- Fluorine is more reactive than chlorine because fluorine has a smaller atomic size, so its nucleus attracts electrons more
strongly, giving it a higher tendency to gain an electron compared to chlorine.
17. Write any two factors that determine the chemical reactivity of metal.
Ans:- Two factors that determine the chemical reactivity of a metal are,
1. Atomic size: Metals with larger atomic size lose their valence electrons more easily, increasing reactivity.
2. Ionization energy: Metals with lower ionization energy can lose electrons more readily, making them more reactive.
18. The size of atoms increases on going from top to bottom in a group of the periodic table. Why?
Ans:- The size of atoms increases from top to bottom in a group because new electron shells are added in each successive
element, increasing the distance between the nucleus and the outermost electrons, which increases atomic size despite the
increase in nuclear charge.
19. Hydrogen is non-metal but it is kept with metal in the modern periodic table. Why?
Ans:- Hydrogen is a non-metal but is placed in Group 1 (with alkali metals) because it has one electron in its outermost shell,
similar to alkali metals, and can lose this electron to form a positive ion (H⁺), showing a similarity in chemical behavior.
20. The metallic characters of elements decrease and nonmetallic characters increases on going from left to right of a period
in the modern periodic table. Why?
Ans:- The metallic character of elements decreases and nonmetallic character increases from left to right in a period because
the atomic size decreases and the nucleus holds the electrons more strongly, making it harder to lose electrons and easier to
gain electrons.
